key_reasoning.reason: Four components across API models (assistant.py), service (assistant_service.py build_agent and resolve call), agent (langgraph_agent.py headroom kwarg and pre-model hook wiring in both single-agent and supervisor chains), and persistence (migration). Builtin subagent clones inherit the config, so the agent path is shared across sub-assistants.

The hook runs on every LLM call and makes a blocking sidecar call bounded by HEADROOM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, so it is on the hot path with moderate performance impact. Fail-open behaviour, the kill switch and the feature flag give rollback, but the balanced and aggressive strategies can reduce provider prompt-cache hits. The closest precedent is the hedging_config JSONB pattern and the existing pre-model hook chain, so the risk is not novel.

10 files changed (4 modified: AGENTS.md, langgraph_agent.py, assistant.py, assistant_service.py; 6 new: the guide, the migration and 4 test modules) across the agents, service, rest_api/models, external/alembic and tests trees. 815 insertions and 0 deletions, so the change is additive.

Four layers are touched: API/model (AssistantRequest and Assistant headroom_config field), Service (AssistantService.build_agent resolution and gating), Agent (LangGraphAgent kwarg and hook composition) and DB-Persistence (Alembic add_column on assistants). The schema change is a single additive nullable JSONB column, not a data migration, so it is not treated as a significant schema change. The only external call is through the existing slice 1 hook, and that is not changed here.
